name: SN Wave Runner
description: A personal watercraft for the Great Lakes — fast, agile, and a staple of Tier 3-4 recreation. The Wave Runner is the motorcycle of the water, accessible enough for middle-tier residents to own and fun enough to build a lifestyle around. The lakefront culture of weekend Wave Runner riders is one of GLMZ's more human scenes — people actually enjoying something, even if the water quality requires a decontamination rinse afterward.
common_usage: Recreation, lakefront patrol (budget security), personal watercraft racing, weekend leisure.
story_hooks: A Wave Runner rider discovers their GPS maps show a landmass in the lake that doesn't exist above water — but something is there below the surface
The Wave Runner racing community stumbles onto a smuggling route and has to decide whether to report it or profit from it
physical_description: The Wave Runner is a sleek personal watercraft with a reinforced polymer hull in faded pearl-gray, its surface etched with salt corrosion and micro-abrasions from years of Great Lakes use. Twin jet intakes flank a narrow operator's seat, with a wraparound windscreen of scratched composite plastic and exposed aluminum tubing at the frame joints. Control systems are mounted on reinforced handlebars with worn grip tape, and the fuel access panel bears faded Sterling-Nakamura insignia half-obscured by weathering.
visual_prompt: sleek personal watercraft, faded pearl-gray hull with salt corrosion and micro-scratches, twin jet intakes, reinforced polymer and aluminum frame, worn composite windscreen, gritty neo-noir aesthetic, detailed product photography, dark industrial background, moody lighting, weathered recreation tech, Great Lakes industrial decay
